mostWorthwhile.text: Checking the citation against the edition’s page count was the most worthwhile: it gave a clear, practical way to test apparent scholarly authority.

leastWorthwhile.text: The photo comparison repeated the broader point that context affects interpretation, though its political example added a useful distinction.

surprise.text: Identical words can become a different work through a later author’s context, even when their wording is settled.

arbitrary.text: The link from an edition showing textual doubts to Menard’s authorship initially felt less direct; the result clarified the distinction between wording and interpretation.

continue.text: I would continue: the concrete checks on citations and photographs made questions about evidence and interpretation engaging.
